mtw.name: MTW

nmbJacket.name: NM-B cable jacket
nmbJacket.material: PVC outer jacket of a non-metallic-sheathed cable

thhnThwn2.name: THHN/THWN-2
thhnThwn2.material: PVC insulation with an extruded nylon jacket

sources.citation: Conductor temperature ratings of the types as public manufacturers' specification sheets state them for wire listed to the UL standards, cited by number only (UL 83 for THHN/THWN-2, UL 44 for XHHW-2, UL 1063 for MTW, UL 719 for NM-B), paraphrased: THHN 90 °C in dry locations; THWN-2 and XHHW-2 90 °C in wet or dry locations; MTW 90 °C dry and 60 °C wet; NM-B 90 °C, which is the rating of the cable's conductors, not of the jacket compound (the jacket row carries the cable's rating). Not taken from the NEC's conductor-insulation table. How much current a rating allows is derived by the thermal model (D6), never stored.
NFPA 70-2023 Art. 334.12 (uses not permitted; cited by number and paraphrased) keeps NM cable out of wet and damp locations, so the NM-B jacket row has no wet rating.

Thermal conductivity of PVC about 0.16 to 0.20 W/(m·K) (0.18 is taken, mid-band) and of nylon 6/6 about 0.25 W/(m·K), from a plastics distributor's published thermal-property table (read by electrical-realism-reviewer in the P3 source pre-audit), paraphrased. Compound-to-compound spread is about as large as the difference between the two.

game-design choice inside real constructions: XHHW-2 is a single XLPE layer and an NM-B jacket a single PVC layer; MTW is made both as plain PVC and with a nylon jacket, and the single-layer variant is taken here. So these rows have no outer jacket layer.

game-design: unverified, so not a measurement. XLPE thermal conductivity of about 0.29 W/(m·K) appears only in a secondary source (a field-simulation package's material library); the primary reference, IEC 60287-2-1, is paywalled and was not read. Replace with a verified figure, as a new table version, when one is found.

game-design judgement: a total emissivity of 0.9 for every insulation and jacket surface. An infrared-thermometer maker's emissivity table gives about 0.93 for PVC (read in the P3 source pre-audit); colours and nylon differ a little. Radiation is kept because it carries 20 to 30 % of a small conductor's heat in free air (D6).
